newsitem.title: GERMANY: Boss says expects H1 sales to climb 5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Boss says expects H1 sales to climb 5 pct.

text.p: STUTTGART, Germany, Jan 22 (Retuer) - German clothing company Hugo Boss AG expects to see sales in the first half of this year climb five percent to 475 million marks ($289 million), board member Joerg-Viggo Mueller said late Tuesday evening.
Mueller said sales last year climbed 10.5 percent to 995.5 million marks, largely on the back of stronger sales abroad which climbed 13.9 percent while domestic sales grew 4.9 percent.
The Boss executive did not provide specific profit figures for 1996, but said "In general, the influence of higher sales should have a positive impact on profits."
Boss says expects H1 sales to climb 5 pct
Mueller said two brands introduced in 1993 posted strong sales growth in 1996.

Boss's line of clothing for younger customers, the Hugo brand, produced sales growth of 42 percent to 41.3 million marks. Sales of the company's up-market Baldessarini band, meanwhile, climbed 39 percent to 18.7 million marks.
The designated new Boss chairman, Joachim Vogt, said that he would not alter the company's main sales strategy. "It is clear that we will build up and continue our strategy," Vogt said.
Boss had recently announced that current chairman Peter Littmann will step down when his contract expires at the end of the year.
